cohort: The study included 4851 children aged 6-9 years from diverse Greek rural and urban regions.
finding: This study found that higher maternal education, family economic status, exclusive breastfeeding, and higher physical activity levels were strong predictors for increased Mediterranean diet adherence, while cesarean delivery and higher birth weight were linked to lower adherence, and higher adherence correlated with lower prevalence of depressive and anxiety symptoms in children aged 6-9 years.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was linked to lower Mediterranean diet adherence in children aged 6-9 years.
cross-section timing: Children aged 6-9 years at the time of the survey
birth_weight: Measured (higher birth weight linked to lower MD adherence)
